statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-57914 is a stack overflow on deeply nested ASN.1 input in Apache Kerby, fixed in Kerby 2.1.2. The kerby-asn1 1.0.1 classes reported here are shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6 in the druid-ranger-security extension and cannot be upgraded on their own. The latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) carries kerby-asn1 2.0.3 and no Kerby 2.1.2 copy. The shaded ASN.1 parser can be reached when the Hadoop client handles Kerberos data in a secured deployment, so reachability has not been ruled out. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x6vc-x4v4-hjhr

CVE-2026-57914 is a stack overflow on deeply nested ASN.1 input in Apache Kerby, fixed in Kerby 2.1.2. The kerby-asn1 1.0.1 classes reported here are shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6 in the druid-ranger-security extension and cannot be upgraded on their own. The latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) carries kerby-asn1 2.0.3 and no Kerby 2.1.2 copy. The shaded ASN.1 parser can be reached when the Hadoop client handles Kerberos data in a secured deployment, so reachability has not been ruled out. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x6vc-x4v4-hjhr

The Kerby 1.0.1 kerby-asn1 classes reported here are copies shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6 and hbase-shaded-client 2.6.0; the image's own Kerby jars are 2.1.2, which includes the fix. No Hadoop or HBase release shades Kerby 2.1.2. The shaded ASN.1 parser can be reached when the Hadoop or HBase client handles Kerberos data in a secured deployment, so reachability has not been ruled out.

The kerby-asn1 classes reported here are copies shaded inside the bundled Hadoop and HBase client jars: Kerby 1.0.1 in hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6 and hbase-shaded-client 2.6.0 (JanusGraph 1.1), and Kerby 2.0.3 in hadoop-client-runtime 3.4.3 and hbase-shaded-client 2.6.6 (JanusGraph 1.2). The image's own Kerby jars are 2.1.2, which includes the fix. No Hadoop or HBase release shades Kerby 2.1.2. The shaded ASN.1 parser can be reached when the Hadoop or HBase client handles Kerberos data in a secured deployment, so reachability has not been ruled out.
